topics.name: Wh-questions to get a given answer
Collocations (make a profit, made a study)
Modals with have (must have, should have, could have)
Past tenses: simple, continuous and perfect

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: When I reached the station, the train has already left.
When I reached the station, the train had already left.
When I reached the station, the train had already leave.
questions.rule: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect: had left.

options: Hari did a big mistake that night.
Hari made a big mistake that night.
Hari took a big mistake that night.
questions.rule: We always say make a mistake, not do or take a mistake.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After did, use the base form of the verb: did ... hide.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The story is in the past: while Anil was sleeping, Hari crept up (past of creep).

questions.after: just sold a book to a publisher.
questions.rule: In reported speech after said, the tense moves back: has sold becomes had sold.

questions.after: when Hari sat under the clock tower.
questions.rule: After the verb raining we need an adverb: heavily.
Wh-question in the past: Wh-word + did + subject + base verb.

options: I lives near the Jumna Sweet Shop.
I live near the Jumna Sweet Shop.
I living near the Jumna Sweet Shop.
questions.rule: Answer a do question in the simple present; with I use the base form: live.

chat: Why were you late for school?
options: The bus has gone before I reached the stop.
The bus had go before I reached the stop.
The bus had gone before I reached the stop.
questions.rule: The bus went first, so use the past perfect: had gone.

questions.source: Anil said to Hari, "I can't pay you."
options: Anil told Hari that I couldn't pay you.
Anil told to Hari that he couldn't pay him.
Anil told Hari that he couldn't pay him.
questions.rule: said to becomes told; I/you become he/him; can't moves back to couldn't.

options: The meal must had been terrible.
The meal must have be terrible.
The meal must have been terrible.
questions.rule: A guess about the past: must have + past participle (been).

options: What Hari did learn from Anil?
What did Hari learn from Anil?
What did Hari learned from Anil?
questions.rule: Question order: What + did + subject + base verb.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: should have is always followed by the past participle: should have jumped.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Present perfect continuous: has been + working, for an action going on since a past time.

questions.prompt: Choose the wh-word that gets this answer.
questions.after: did Hari go to the station? To catch the Lucknow Express.
questions.rule: The answer gives a reason or purpose (to catch ...), so ask with Why.

questions.after: a profit of about a rupee a day.
questions.rule: The fixed pair is make a profit.
A yes/no question is reported with if and statement order: if I could cook.

chat: I can't find my phone anywhere!
options: You must left it in the classroom.
You must have leave it in the classroom.
You must have left it in the classroom.
questions.rule: A guess about the past: must have + past participle (left).

questions.prompt: Make a wh-question to get the word in capitals.
options: What did the poor man show?
What did the poor man showed?
questions.rule: Ask about a thing with What; past question: did + subject + base verb.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: Past continuous: was sleeping. The story is in the past: before Anil woke up.

options: Anil asked Hari what was his name.
Anil asked Hari what his name was.
Anil asked Hari what is his name.
questions.rule: A reported question uses statement order: what his name was.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After does, use the base form: does Hari change.

questions.before: The train was moving slowly. Hari
questions.after: jumped into it, but he hesitated.
questions.rule: A past chance that was not used: could have + past participle.

questions.before: By the time Hari reached the station, the Lucknow Express
questions.rule: By the time + past: the earlier action takes the past perfect, had started.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence that shows a strong guess about the past.
questions.rule: Strong guess about the past: must have + past participle (known).

chat: What did Anil say in the morning?
options: He said that he has made some money the day before.
He said that he had made some money the day before.
He said that he had make some money the day before.
questions.rule: Reported speech moves back: made becomes had made; yesterday becomes the day before.

options: I did my best, but I made two silly mistakes.
I made my best, but I did two silly mistakes.
I did my best, but I did two silly mistakes.
questions.rule: Fixed pairs: do your best, make a mistake.

questions.source: Hari said to Anil, "Can you feed me?"
options: Hari asked Anil that could he feed him.
Hari asked Anil if he could feed him.
Hari asked Anil can he feed him.
questions.rule: Yes/no question: asked + if, statement order, can becomes could.

questions.prompt: Make a wh-question to get the words in capitals.
questions.source: Hari made tea IN THE MORNING.
questions.rule: Ask about time with When; past question: did + subject + base verb (make).

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: to + base verb: to teach. Hari (one person): was. Comparison: more ... than.

options: How long Hari had been working for Anil?
How long had Hari been worked for Anil?
How long had Hari been working for Anil?
questions.rule: Question order: had + subject + been + -ing.

options: Anil told Hari to not wasting the money.
Anil told Hari don't waste the money.
Anil told Hari not to waste the money.
questions.rule: A negative command is reported with told + person + not to + verb.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After a modal (could), use have, never has: could have handed.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The subject is Hari, not scars, so the verb is singular: was.
A reported request: requested + person + to + verb.
make a study of something means to observe it carefully.
Question order: Why + will + subject + base verb (be).

questions.source: Anil said to Hari, "Today we'll start writing sentences."
options: Anil told Hari that we would start writing sentences that day.
Anil told Hari that they will start writing sentences today.
Anil told Hari that they would start writing sentences that day.
questions.rule: we becomes they, will becomes would, today becomes that day.

questions.source: I am sure that Anil knew about the theft.
options: Anil must have known about the theft.
Anil must know about the theft.
Anil must have knew about the theft.
questions.rule: Sure about the past: must have + past participle (known).

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: Past story: Hari didn't have, Hari was alone. Comparisons use than.

options: If Hari would have caught the train, he would have reached Lucknow.
If Hari had caught the train, he will have reached Lucknow.
If Hari had caught the train, he would have reached Lucknow.
questions.rule: Imagined past: If + had + past participle, would have + past participle.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Money goes with make: make money, make a profit, make a mistake. So: made a lot of money.

questions.after: we had finished the character sketch.
questions.rule: A reported yes/no question is joined with whether (or if).
Whose + noun comes first, then did + subject + base verb.

chat: I failed the test. I didn't study at all.
options: You should have study. You'll do better next time.
You should have studied. You'll do better next time.
You should studied. You'll do better next time.
questions.rule: Advice about the past: should have + past participle (studied).

chat: What did the station master tell you?
options: He told me that the Lucknow Express had left ten minutes before.
He told me that the Lucknow Express has left ten minutes ago.
He said me that the Lucknow Express had left ten minutes before.
questions.rule: Use told me (not said me); move back to had left; ago becomes before.

questions.source: As soon as Hari reached the platform, the train moved out.
options: No sooner Hari reached the platform than the train moved out.
No sooner did Hari reached the platform than the train moved out.
No sooner did Hari reach the platform than the train moved out.
questions.rule: No sooner takes question order: did + subject + base verb, then than.

questions.source: Hari said, "What a fool I have been!"
options: Hari exclaimed that he had been a great fool.
Hari exclaimed that what a fool he had been.
Hari exclaimed that he has been a great fool.
questions.rule: An exclamation becomes a statement: exclaimed that, drop what, and have been becomes had been.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: had reported (past participle). The story is past: paid. An adverb describes paid: regularly.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: We make a study of something. After to, use the base verb: fails to notice.
